title: EMCU students gather at Education Ministry over disrupted classes and examinations
location: Ministry of Education and Training, Mbabane
scope: One reported student gathering at the ministry; distinct from lecturer/staff labor strike and campus disputes.
organizer: Eswatini Medical Christian University students; student leadership represented the group.

state_target.target: Minister and Ministry of Education and Training
state_target.evidence: Students approached the minister/ministry to seek intervention over class and exam-calendar disruption.

demands_original: Students sought help over missed classes/exams and disruption of academic calendar; asked minister to engage university board.
participants_original: More than 50 EMCU students (one local newspaper report).
threshold_50_evidence: The source explicitly reports more than 50 students gathered at the ministry.

start_date.summary: Article published August 20 says students arrived 'yesterday', August 19.

end_date.summary: No end time or duration reported.

location.summary: Gathering was at the Ministry of Education and Training in Mbabane.

scope.summary: Single ministry gathering by EMCU students; no evidence it was a nationwide coordinated event.

state_target.summary: Students presented grievances to the education minister and sought ministerial intervention.

participants_original.summary: Local report says more than 50 EMCU students.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Explicit count exceeds 50 at the named site.

state_response.summary: Minister said he would engage the university board; no outcome or resolution shown. Police access restriction is reported, but dispersal is not established.

notes: Do not merge with lecturer/staff strike or other campus boycotts. The minister’s promise is not evidence the underlying issue was resolved.
open_questions: Independent attendance corroboration is unavailable in this packet.
No closure date or post-gathering continuation established.

title: William Pitcher College students protest learning and hostel conditions
scope: One prolonged on-campus student protest beginning during August; no evidence for another public site.
organizer: William Pitcher College students; student electoral officer quoted by the local outlet.

state_target.target: College leadership/administration; the source does not show a direct demand to national government
state_target.evidence: Students protested learning conditions and called for college closure; report describes action and response by the college principal, not government.

demands_original: Students protested an allegedly non-conducive learning environment: broken toilets, no security for students walking at night, cold showers, and malfunctioning Wi-Fi; placards called for college closure.
threshold_50_evidence: No student count or qualitative crowd estimate reported.

start_date.summary: Reports say protest began 'last week Monday' relative to 27 August publication; exact day not printed. Month is August.

end_date.summary: Classes were suspended and students ordered to vacate on 26 August; this does not establish the protest’s closure.

scope.summary: Reports describe one prolonged college protest; no other-site actions shown.

organizer.summary: Students acted collectively; no formal organizer identified.

state_target.summary: Immediate target appears to be college administration/conditions; no explicit national-government demand.

demands.summary: Learning and hostel conditions; students called for college closure.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Threshold of 50 simultaneous protesters not established.

protester_violence.summary: Local reports say students set fires and damaged college property as protest escalated.

state_response.summary: College principal suspended in-person learning; no state response in the codebook dimensions is established.

notes: Two local publications report overlapping facts but independence/origin relation is unresolved; do not count as independent without source genealogy. A public college's status alone does not establish that demands were aimed at government.
open_questions: Whether students demanded action from the government, rather than college administration.
Exact start day and actual protest end date.
